title: Japan launches second US military payload to monitor space above Indo-Pacific
summary: Japan has launched its second US military payload, QZS-7, designed to monitor space above the Indo-Pacific region. Data from QZS-7 and its predecessor, QZS-6, will feed into the US Space Surveillance Network, enhancing space domain awareness for the 18th Space Defense Squadron.

title: The Past and Future of AI Scientists
summary: arXiv:2608.14407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a survey of the past and future of AI Scientists: machines capable of automating science. AI Scientists can originate hypotheses, deduce their consequences, design and execute experiments, interpret their results, and revise their beliefs. Such systems are …
detail: This paper surveys the evolving field of "AI Scientists," machines designed to automate the entire scientific process. These systems can generate hypotheses, design and execute experiments, interpret results, and refine their understanding. Early examples include Adam, which made novel discoveries, and Eve, which established the architecture for self-driving laboratories. The paper highlights how modern advancements like foundation models, autonomous agents, and laboratory robotics now enable the creation of far more general AI Scientists. The primary challenge is no longer automating individual scientific components, but integrating diverse AI capabilities—neural learning, logic, mathematics, causal reasoning, simulation, experimental design, and robotics—into cohesive systems. This development matters because AI Scientists have the potential to significantly accelerate the pace of scientific discovery, making research faster and more efficient across various fields by automating complex and time-consuming tasks.

title: Agentao: A Governed Local-First Runtime for Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: arXiv:2608.13574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly operate as execution systems that invoke tools, modify local state, use persistent memory, and interact with external protocols. These capabilities make agents useful, but they also introduce risks related to over-privileged actions, weak …
detail: This paper introduces Agentao, a new runtime environment designed to enhance the security and governability of tool-using Large Language Model (LLM) agents. As LLM agents increasingly interact with external tools, modify local data, and use persistent memory, they introduce risks such as over-privileged actions, prompt injection vulnerabilities, and uncontrolled side effects. Agentao addresses these concerns through a layered architecture that explicitly separates an agent's proposed actions from their authorized execution. It incorporates a permission-mediated tool system, robust state management, and detailed execution traces to improve auditability and control. This development is crucial because as LLM agents become more integrated into real-world applications, ensuring their safe and secure operation is paramount. Agentao aims to make these powerful autonomous systems more trustworthy and suitable for sensitive tasks by providing explicit mechanisms for oversight and risk mitigation, moving towards more responsible AI deployment.

title: AI Evaluation Should Work With Humans
summary: arXiv:2608.13577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This position paper argues that the dominant paradigm of AI evaluation (which focuses on superhuman autonomous performance and so implicitly targets the goal of replacing humans) is guiding AI development in the wrong direction. Instead, the AI community should pivot to …
detail: This position paper argues that the prevailing approach to evaluating AI systems, which focuses on achieving superhuman autonomous performance and implicitly aims to replace human capabilities, is misdirected. Instead, the authors advocate for a paradigm shift towards evaluating the performance of human-AI teams. This means assessing how effectively AI systems collaborate with humans to achieve shared goals, rather than how well they perform in isolation. This shift matters significantly because it encourages the development of AI systems designed to complement and augment human intelligence, rather than supersede it. By fostering AI that acts as a true partner, this collaborative evaluation approach is expected to lead to more beneficial societal outcomes, promoting AI that enhances human productivity, creativity, and decision-making across various domains, ultimately leading to more robust and ethical AI integration.

title: Active Perception for Embodied Disambiguation
summary: arXiv:2608.13605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Natural language provides robots with a flexible task interface, but target ambiguity in embodied environments arises not only from user intent; it can also result from missing taskrelevant physical evidence in the current observation. Existing interactive …
detail: This paper proposes an active perception framework to help robots resolve ambiguity in natural language commands, especially when crucial physical information is missing or obscured in their environment. Unlike traditional methods that primarily rely on asking the user for clarification, this framework enables robots to actively change their viewpoint or explore the surroundings (active observation) to gather more visual evidence. A vision-language model then decides whether to continue observing, request user clarification, or proceed with the task based on accumulated evidence. This research is important because it significantly enhances the robustness and autonomy of robots interacting with humans in complex, real-world settings. By allowing robots to proactively seek out missing information through physical actions, it reduces the need for constant human intervention, making human-robot interaction more intuitive and efficient, particularly for tasks requiring physical manipulation or navigation in dynamic environments.

title: Reward Machines for Signal Temporal Logic
summary: arXiv:2608.13625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Signal temporal logic (STL) provides a formal language for specifying real-time properties of real-valued observations, along with a quantitative robustness score for monitoring satisfaction. Control synthesis from STL specifications is of interest since manual …
detail: This paper introduces a novel method for training reinforcement learning (RL) agents to adhere to complex, real-time specifications expressed in Signal Temporal Logic (STL). STL provides a formal language for defining desired system behaviors over time, crucial for safety-critical applications. A key challenge in using STL with RL is that the 'robustness score' (quantifying satisfaction) depends on the entire execution history, leading to an intractable state space for long-horizon tasks. The proposed solution constructs a 'timed alternating automaton' from the STL specifications, which efficiently augments the RL agent's state space with automaton locations. This provides an effective memory mechanism and generates Markovian rewards suitable for standard RL frameworks. This work is significant because it makes it more feasible to apply RL to control systems requiring formal guarantees, enabling autonomous systems (like robots or self-driving cars) to learn complex behaviors while reliably satisfying predefined safety and performance specifications, even without precise system models.
